mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the federal funds rate over 3 consecutive months indicates the Federal Reserve is shifting from tightening to easing, lowering discount rates and increasing equity valuation multiples, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day forward returns in > 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS declines for 3 consecutive months, or 20-day returns are not statistically higher than the pre-signal period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% signals a tightening cycle, prompting investors to reduce equity exposure and seek safer assets, which produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX achieves positive 60-day forward returns in > 70% of periods where FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% (rolling 3-month average), or 60-day returns are not statistically lower than pre-signal (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate for 6 consecutive months indicates a prolonged easing stance, compressing discount rates and boosting equity valuation multiples, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day forward returns in > 50% of periods where FEDFUNDS declines for 6 consecutive months, or 5-day returns are not statistically higher than pre-signal (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) above 200,000 jobs indicates a strengthening labor market, prompting higher consumer confidence and equity valuations, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day forward returns in > 60% of periods where PAYEMS exceeds 200,000, or 20-day returns are not statistically higher than pre-signal (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in monthly employment growth below -100,000 jobs signals a weakening labor market, reducing consumer and business confidence and compressing equity valuations, which produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX achieves positive 60-day forward returns in > 70% of periods where PAYEMS falls below -100,000 (rolling 3-month average), or 60-day returns are not statistically lower than pre-signal (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) for 4 consecutive months indicates weakening domestic demand, compressing corporate earnings and equity valuations, which produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day forward returns in > 60% of periods where INDPRO declines for 4 consecutive months, or 20-day returns are not statistically lower than pre-signal (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in industrial production (INDPRO) above 105 indicates strengthening domestic supply capacity, prompting optimism about future growth and equity valuation expansion, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day forward returns in > 70% of periods where INDPRO exceeds 105 (rolling 3-month average), or 60-day returns are not statistically higher than pre-signal (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in residential investment (HOUST) for 3 consecutive months indicates reduced household spending, compressing corporate earnings and equity valuations, which produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day forward returns in > 60% of periods where HOUST declines for 3 consecutive months, or 5-day returns are not statistically lower than pre-signal (t-test p > 0.05).
